object_types.name: Customer

ambiguities.description: The billing system uses the term 'Client' for what is generally treated as the same concept as 'Customer', but the billing team's definition differs: they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid. Is 'Client' truly the same entity type as 'Customer', or a distinct subtype/status (e.g., a Customer who has made a payment)? This affects whether Client should be modeled as a separate concept or constraint on Customer.

source_references.excerpt: In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients." For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: The multiplicity of Order-Product (via order lines) is stated as 'an order contains one or more products' and 'a product can appear in many different orders', implying many-to-many, but it's not explicit whether an order can list the same product on multiple separate lines (with different quantities) or exactly one line per product per SKU. This affects the uniqueness constraint on the ternary fact type.

source_references.excerpt: An order contains one or more products. Each line in the order specifies a product and a quantity. A product can appear in many different orders.

ambiguities.description: No explicit statement addresses whether Order Status changes over time and whether history of status transitions needs to be tracked, or whether only the current status matters. This is modeled as current-state only.

source_references.excerpt: Yes, an order has a status. The possible values are: pending, confirmed, shipped, and delivered. Every order must have a status.

ambiguities.description: It is unclear whether CustomerName uniqueness (at most one name per customer) is truly a business rule or simply an unstated assumption; the transcript only confirms customers have a name as a text field without discussing whether it can change or have multiple values.

source_references.excerpt: Yes, every customer has a name. It's just a text field.

ambiguities.description: The identification of 'quantity' per order line is described only informally ('each line specifies a product and a quantity'); it's unclear if quantity must be a positive integer with any minimum/maximum bounds, or if zero/negative values are disallowed by business rule.
